hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxides change from basic on the left to acidic on the right, and how that affects reaction with water and with acid.
Notice that X has an oxide with no reaction with water but which still forms a salt with HCl, which points to an amphoteric oxide.
Connect the chloride behaviour to charge density, covalent chlorides hydrolyse to give acidic solutions while ionic NaCl simply dissolves.
walkthrough:
**Sort out what the oxide + water tells us**

Think left to right across Period 3. Basic oxides of Na and Mg react with water to give hydroxides. Amphoteric $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and acidic $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and show no reaction. Acidic oxides of P and S react to form acids.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

**Identify X as aluminium**

X oxide shows no reaction with water, so X is $\text{Al}$ or $\text{Si}$. But X oxide reacts with $\text{HCl(aq)}$ to form a chloride salt, so it must be basic or amphoteric.

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check X chloride and identify Y and Z**

$\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic and would not react with an acid, so X cannot be Si. This fits $\text{AlCl}_3$ which hydrolyses in water to give an acidic solution. Y forms a hydroxide and a salt with acid and its chloride just dissolves, so Y is a basic metal oxide of Na or Mg. Z forms an acid and its chloride hydrolyses, so Z is a non-metal like P or S.

**Match to the statements**

Only one pairing gives X as the amphoteric metal with no reaction of its oxide with water but salt formation with acid, Y as a basic oxide forming hydroxide, and Z as an acidic oxide forming acid. That is X as Al and Y as Mg.

options.A: X fits Al: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble (no reaction with water), amphoteric so reacts with HCl to give $\text{AlCl}_3$, and $\text{AlCl}_3$ hydrolyses. Y fits Mg: $\text{MgO}$ is basic, gives $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ with water and $\text{MgCl}_2$ with HCl, while $\text{MgCl}_2$ simply dissolves without vigorous hydrolysis.
options.B: X cannot be Si. $\text{SiO}_2$ has no reaction with water which fits, and $\text{SiCl}_4$ hydrolyses which fits, but $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic and does not react with HCl to form a chloride salt. Acid plus acid gives no reaction.
options.C: Y cannot be Al. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble in water and shows no reaction, it does not form a hydroxide solution. Y clearly forms a hydroxide, so Y is a Group 1 or Group 2 basic oxide, not aluminium.
options.D: Z cannot be Al. Z oxide forms an acid with water, but $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and insoluble with no reaction. Z must be a non-metal acidic oxide such as phosphorus or sulfur.
